text: Your phone rings. This is the FTC. Your number is linked to a crime. Would you stay on the line?
The FTC warned about this exact call on October 22nd. The caller says a phone in your name is running scams overseas.
Cooperate or your number gets deactivated.
My number? I don't even have a phone!
So why does a government call end with a payment?
First, they pass you to a fake police officer, then you're told you're under arrest, and
then comes the part that costs you.
To clear your name, you pay a security deposit.
Each step hands you to someone more official, so it feels more real.
The FTC says real staff never ask for money, never threaten your phone, and never ask for
So the only thing to deactivate is the call.
Comment. Has a fake agency ever called you? This is Money Mirage. Follow for more.
